message.content:
Here are some of the most popular books written by J.K. Rowling:

| Title | Year Published | Notes |
|-------|----------------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | First book in the Harry Potter series; introduces Harry, Hogwarts, and the wizarding world. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second installment; explores the mystery of the Chamber and the basilisk. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Third book; introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Fourth book; features the Triwizard Tournament. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Fifth book; focuses on Dumbledore’s Army and the rise of Voldemort. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Sixth book; delves into Voldemort’s backstory and Horcruxes. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Final book; concludes the epic saga. |
| **Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them** | 2001 | Companion book to the Harry Potter films; includes a fictional textbook on magical creatures. |
| **Quidditch Through the Ages** | 2001 | Another companion book detailing the history of Quidditch. |
| **The Tales of Beedle the Bard** | 2008 | A collection of wizarding fairy tales. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel; a political drama set in a small English town. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | Debut novel under the pseudonym Robert Galbraith; a detective mystery featuring private investigator Cormoran Strike. |
| **The Silkworm** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable published as a free online book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |

These titles span Rowling’s most famous works, her companion books for the Harry Potter films, her first adult novel, and her detective series written under a pseudonym.
